hints: Notice the vertical axis: positive displacement means the air molecule has moved to the right and negative means it has moved to the left at that distance.
Recall that air pressure is lowest at a rarefaction, where molecules on either side have moved away from that point and the air is least crowded.
Compare the zero-crossings B and D by looking at the displacement just to the left and just to the right of each point to see which one has molecules pulling apart.
walkthrough: Identify the given graph: it is displacement of air against distance, with up as displaced right and down as displaced left, and A, B, C, D marked along one wavelength.
State the physical rule: sound is a longitudinal wave, so high pressure is a compression where molecules move together and low pressure is a rarefaction where molecules move apart.
Test point B where the curve falls through zero: just left of B displacement is to the right and just right of B displacement is to the left, so both sides move toward B and the air is compressed.
Test point D where the curve rises through zero: just left of D displacement is to the left and just right of D displacement is to the right, so both sides move away from D and the air is rarefied.
Therefore the lowest pressure is at the rarefaction at D. This is option D

options.A: At A displacement to the right is maximum, so neighbouring molecules are displaced by almost the same amount and spacing is almost unchanged, giving near-normal pressure.
options.B: At B molecules on the left are displaced right and molecules on the right are displaced left, so they crowd together in a compression where pressure is highest.
options.C: At C displacement to the left is maximum, so neighbouring molecules move together with little change in spacing, giving near-normal pressure.
options.D: At D molecules on the left are displaced left and molecules on the right are displaced right, so they spread apart in a rarefaction where pressure is lowest.
